title: Counting Permutations with Exactly k Fixed Points

problemStatement.formal: \#\{\sigma \in S_n : \sigma \text{ has exactly } k \text{ fixed points}\} = \binom{n}{k} D(n-k)
problemStatement.plain: Proves S(n,k) = C(n,k)·D(n-k): the number of permutations of n elements with exactly k fixed points equals the binomial coefficient C(n,k) times the derangement number D(n-k). Verified for n=3,4,5 via native_decide. Proved via bijection between {σ | support = S} and derangements of S.
whyMatters: Connects fixed-point counting in permutations to derangements by choosing the fixed points and deranging the remaining elements.
Provides a natural bijective route for the formula S(n,k) = C(n,k)·D(n-k).

# Knowledge Base: derangements-oq-02

Insights accumulated during research on this problem.

---

## Problem Understanding

The target is the formula S(n,k) = C(n,k) * D(n-k): the number of permutations of n elements with exactly k fixed points equals the number of ways to choose those fixed points times the number of derangements of the remaining elements.

The local problem statement says cases n=3,4,5 were verified by native_decide and names a bijective route between permutations with a fixed support and derangements on the complementary set.

---

## Insights

- The counting argument should separate the choice of fixed points from the derangement of the remaining elements.
